label: Tropical nights at +2.7 °C (TRACC 2050)
legend_note: Nights a year when the temperature never drops below 20 °C — the nights that stop bodies and buildings recovering from a hot day — at +2.7 °C, the warming France plans for 2050 (TRACC). Median of 17 bias-corrected regional simulations (DRIAS, Explore2), 20-year average, weighted by where residents live. From the 8 km grid with no altitude correction, so a valley town below its cell's mean altitude reads a little low. The popup has the model range, the change since 1976–2005 and +4 °C.

label: Days reaching 35 °C at +2.7 °C (TRACC 2050)
legend_note: Days a year reaching 35 °C at +2.7 °C (TRACC 2050): the heat at which outdoor work, sleep and older people's health suffer. Median of 17 bias-corrected regional simulations (DRIAS, Explore2), 20-year average, weighted by where residents live. An 8 km grid without altitude correction, and a median that smooths extremes: the hottest years will bring several times this. The popup has the model range, the change since 1976–2005 and +4 °C.

label: Dry-soil days at +2.7 °C (TRACC 2050)

fields.name: sol_sec_2050
fields.label: Days with dry soil (soil wetness index below 0.4) at +2.7 °C (ensemble median)

legend_note: Days a year when the soil is dry — Météo-France's soil wetness index below 0.4 — at +2.7 °C (TRACC 2050). Dry soil is agricultural drought, fire-prone vegetation and, on clay, the shrinkage that cracks houses: pair it with the clay layer. Median of the Explore2 SIM2 hydrology runs (DRIAS), 20-year average, weighted by where residents live. The popup has the ensemble maximum, the change since 1976–2005 and +4 °C.

fields.name: feux_meteo_20
fields.label: At +2.0 °C (median), the fire model's present-day weather

legend_note: Days a year when hot, dry, windy weather makes a fire hard to control — the Fire Weather Index at 40 or above — at +2.7 °C (TRACC 2050). It measures the weather only: not how much vegetation there is to burn, nor how often fires start. That is why it underrates the pine forests of the Landes, where humid Atlantic weather hides a large fuel load. Median of 17 bias-corrected simulations (DRIAS, Explore2), weighted by where residents live.
